rationale: Unattested lexeme; context (sun-ship simile + 'great Spirit dwells within') requires a glowing/containing vessel. Possibly related to ⲃⲣⲏⲣⲉ 'kiln.'
Verb of indwelling/containment. Stem unclear; possibly Lycopolitan reflex of ⲱϣ-stem (be abundant, abide) or a containment-verb. Used of the great Spirit within the furnace-ship.
Tentatively read from root ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine, radiate.' Used of the First Man's radiant presence in the Land of Sweetness/Light. Confidence low.
From ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'to seal, stamp.' Technical term for the typological correspondence: the five body-parts of the King of Darkness ARE the imprint/seal of the five archonic creature-kinds.
Discourse-introducer parallel to ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ. Possibly a Lycopolitan compound: ⲁ-ⲍⲛ-ⲛⲁⲩ-ⲥ 'at the hour' = 'at this moment also.' Confidence low.

Body-part term filling the fifth slot in the King of Darkness anatomical schema. From context: after head/wings/hands-feet/belly, the fifth body-part is loins/tail, corresponding to fish (water-world).
Variant orthography of accumulated ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ. ⲝ-for-ⲭ orthographic variation in Lycopolitan.
Lycopolitan qualitative of ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'sit.' Standard narrative-frame opener: 'as the apostle was sitting in the gathering.'
Indefinite plural article ⲍⲛ̄- + agent-noun ⲣⲉϥ-ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'one who chooses.' Paired with ⲣⲉϩⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'redeemers' in the disciples' double mandate.
